solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Very dry American senator in Rome once

parts.note: brut is the label for very dry champagne

explanation.surface: A parched US senator on a trip to Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American senator' looks like one unit, but American goes with the wordplay and the senator belongs to ancient Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Brutus, one of Caesar's assassins, sat in the Roman Senate.

clue.text: Native of Baltic State stopping debauchee's game

indicators.note: stopping is taken as plugging, so the native fills a gap in the debauchee

parts.note: a roue is a debauched man
a Lett is a person from Latvia

explanation.surface: A Latvian puts an end to a rake's gambling.
explanation.definitionFit: Roulette is a casino gambling game with a spinning wheel.

clue.text: Islander's cry of pleasure welcomed by famous artist

definitions.note: read as islander is: the definition is the noun islander

indicators.note: being welcomed by means being taken in, so the cry goes inside the artist

parts.note: Titian was a Venetian Renaissance painter
ah is a cry of pleasure

explanation.surface: An island native's delighted greeting to a great painter.
explanation.walkthrough: Gauguin painted Tahiti, so a famous artist welcoming islanders seems right, but here it is Titian.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tahitian comes from Tahiti, an island in French Polynesia.

clue.text: Desire the name of this transport across the pond?

definitions.text: Desire the name of this transport across the pond?

parts.words: Desire the name of this transport across the pond?
parts.note: Tennessee Williams' play is about a tram named Desire in New Orleans; across the pond means in America

explanation.surface: A wish to name an American vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desire' looks like a verb but is the name of the vehicle in A Streetcar Named Desire; 'across the pond' means in the US, where a tram has this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans call a tram running on rails in the street by this name.

clue.text: Steal whiskey for large singer

indicators.note: whiskey stands in for large, so one letter is swapped for another in the word for steal

parts.note: half-inch is Cockney rhyming slang for pinch, i.e. steal
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
W is whiskey in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A thief pockets a bottle of whiskey in place of something big.
explanation.walkthrough: HALF-INCH rhymes with pinch, so in Cockney rhyming slang it means steal; swapping its L for W gives HAWFINCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A hawfinch is a songbird, and birds are often called singers in crosswords.

clue.text: Fairy-tale siblings represented in Helen's grand tale?

indicators.note: represented is read as presented anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman named Helen tells a grand story about a brother and sister.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grimm brothers' tale tells of a brother and sister lost in a forest who find a witch's gingerbread house.

clue.text: Sack member producing dangerous weapon

parts.note: to sack someone is to fire them
an arm is a limb or member

explanation.surface: Dismissing a club member who brings in a deadly weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A firearm is a gun, such as a rifle or pistol.

clue.text: Knight of sound mind beheaded citizen

parts.note: N is the chess notation for knight

indicators.note: beheaded means losing the head, the first letter

parts.note: a rational person is of sound mind

explanation.surface: A sane knight losing his head on the block.
explanation.definitionFit: A national of a country is one of its citizens.

clue.text: Eccentric had a nice ranch — in Mexico, possibly

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A quirky person had a lovely ranch in Mexico.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacienda is a large estate or ranch in Spanish-speaking countries.

clue.text: Protestant with stringed instrument managed to capture hearts

indicators.note: capturing something means holding it inside, so the hearts letter goes within the other pieces

parts.note: a lute is a plucked stringed instrument
H is the card-suit abbreviation for hearts
ran, as in ran a business, means managed

explanation.surface: A churchgoing minstrel wins over audiences with his lute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To capture' suggests only the managed word does the capturing, but the hearts letter actually lands inside the instrument word.
explanation.definitionFit: Lutherans belong to the Protestant church founded on Martin Luther's teaching.

clue.text: Judge's wine imbibed by molecular biologist briefly

definitions.note: read as judge is: the definition is the noun judge

indicators.note: something imbibed is drunk in, so the wine goes inside the shortened scientist
briefly means cut short, losing the last letter of the scientist's name

parts.note: Francis Crick co-discovered the structure of DNA
IT is Italian vermouth, as in gin and it

explanation.surface: A judge's glass of wine downed by a famous scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: Gin and it is a cocktail of gin with Italian vermouth, hence IT; CRIC (CRICK without K) takes it in to make CR-IT-IC.
explanation.definitionFit: A reviewer or critic is someone who judges the quality of work.

clue.text: Arty type recalled main article, having time and energy

indicators.note: recalled is taken as called back, so the word for main runs backwards

parts.note: the main is the open sea
the is the definite article
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An artistic person reminiscing about a key essay and having plenty of time and energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' looks like an adjective, but it is the noun meaning sea, turned round to AES.
explanation.definitionFit: An aesthete is a person devoted to beauty and the arts.

clue.text: High wind trapping fighting men in great numbers

indicators.note: trapping means holding inside, so the soldiers are enclosed by the wind

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A storm pinning down soldiers in large numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Galore is a postpositive adjective for in abundance, as in prizes galore.

clue.text: Old word revealing a right rift around India!

indicators.note: the rift goes around the India letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a chasm is a deep rift
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An antique term exposing a serious split concerning India.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaism is an expression that has fallen out of current use.

clue.text: Turn up with baked food at church? A fine example!

parts.note: to turn up is to show up, appear
a pie is baked food
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Turning up at church with a home-baked pie.
explanation.definitionFit: A showpiece is an outstanding example put on display.

clue.text: Aquatic bird shot for speaker

indicators.note: for a speaker means as heard, so the word is spelt as it sounds

parts.note: a shot, as in have a go, is a turn

explanation.surface: A water bird gunned down for someone giving a talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' reads as killed by a gun but means a go, a turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Terns are seabirds that dive for fish.

clue.text: Bill you reportedly delayed, set out systematically

parts.note: a tab is a bill, as in pick up the tab

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the word is written as it sounds

parts.note: the letter U sounds like you
late means delayed

explanation.surface: Your bill came late, laid out in order.
explanation.definitionFit: To tabulate is to arrange data in a table, systematically.

clue.text: Single verse cutting about deceased kinsman

parts.note: re means about, concerning

indicators.note: cutting into means going inside, so single and verse go within the deceased word

parts.note: the late means the deceased
I, the Roman numeral, is one

explanation.surface: A single verse dropped from a eulogy for a dead relative.
explanation.walkthrough: IV goes into LATE: RE + LAT-IV-E.
explanation.definitionFit: A relative is a family member, someone of your kin.

clue.text: Lamb primarily associated with priest

parts.note: Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: A sacrificial lamb linked with a priest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lamb' is not the animal but Charles Lamb, the essayist.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Lamb signed his Essays of Elia with this pen name.

clue.text: Finally diagnose brief illness through smells?

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so each of the two words gives its last letter

parts.note: flu is an illness
via means through, by way of

explanation.surface: Can a doctor diagnose a short bout of illness by its odour?
explanation.definitionFit: Effluvia are unpleasant odours or vapours given off by something.

clue.text: During school time it's temporarily suspended

definitions.note: the verb sense is suspended for a while: the definition is read as stop for a time

parts.note: in means during, as in in the night
a term is a period of the school year
it is given as written; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: Something is put on hold during the school term.
explanation.definitionFit: To intermit is to stop or pause for a while before resuming.

clue.text: Dealings shelved? It's a compromise

parts.note: trade means commercial dealings
a plan that is shelved is off

explanation.surface: Business talks postponed leading to a middle way.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade-off is a balance struck between competing aims, giving up one thing for another.

clue.text: Poles carried in characteristic conveyance

indicators.note: being carried in means being held inside, so the poles go within the characteristic

parts.note: a trait is a characteristic
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Polish people transported in a typical vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Transit is the carrying of goods or people from place to place.

clue.text: Posh headgear rejected by a North American statesman

parts.note: U means upper-class, as in U and non-U

indicators.note: rejected is taken as thrown back, so the headgear runs backwards

parts.note: a hat is headgear

explanation.surface: A US politician refuses to wear a fancy hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Statesman' is a pun: not a politician but a man from one of the States.
explanation.definitionFit: A Utahan is a resident of Utah, one of the United States.

clue.text: Drove back the Spanish in place surrounded by grass

indicators.note: being surrounded by the grass puts the rest inside that plant word

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass

indicators.note: in places the Spanish article within the place abbreviation

parts.note: el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Fighting off Spanish troops dug into a grassy spot.
explanation.walkthrough: EL goes into PL to make PELL, which goes into REED: RE-PELL-ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To repel attackers is to push them back.

clue.text: Lyrical piece a Portuguese-speaking city thus presented

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is in Brazil, where Portuguese is spoken
so means thus

explanation.surface: A song staged in a Brazilian city.
explanation.definitionFit: An arioso is a melodic passage in opera, between recitative and aria.

clue.text: Book couple's got about little folk mostly male

indicators.note: the couple has got itself around the rest, holding it inside

parts.note: a couple is two; the 's is read as has

indicators.note: mostly means not all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: elves are the little folk of folklore

explanation.surface: A pair of books about fairies, nearly all of them men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' here is not a volume but a book size; 'couple's got about' means the pair has wrapped itself around the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelvemo is a book size in which each sheet is folded into twelve leaves.

clue.text: Exciting item in sports programme for unfit layabouts originally

parts.note: each contest on a sports day is an event

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so each word gives its first letter

explanation.surface: A thrilling race on the sports day bill for out-of-shape idlers.
explanation.definitionFit: An eventful time is full of incident, lively rather than dull.

clue.text: Game in farm vehicle caught by East European?

indicators.note: being caught by means being held, so the vehicle sits inside the two letters

parts.note: a cart is a farm vehicle

explanation.surface: A game played in a hay cart by an Eastern European.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecarte is a French card game for two players.
